column1: # THE USAGE-JOURNAL PRODUCER ROSTER -- the DENOMINATOR, written down.
# Read by scripts/verify_usage_journal_producers.py. One row per producer the
# usage-journal contract declares. The contract is
# HR015 launch/USAGE_JOURNAL_CONTRACT.md, section "WHAT EACH REPO OWES" plus the
# sentence immediately below that table ("The daemon already writes `answering`
# for the chat path.").
# WHY A ROSTER AND NOT ">= 1 ENRICHING RECORD"
# The contract's own gate paragraph asks for "at least one `enriching` record
# and at least one `ingesting` record". That predicate is a GOLDEN CASE: three
# repos owe `enriching`, so one of them writing satisfies it forever while the
# other two are dark. The panel then shows a smaller number, which reads as a
# quiet month rather than a broken pipeline -- the exact silent-failure shape
# the contract says it exists to stop, rebuilt inside its own gate.
# A denominator cannot be inferred from a journal, because a producer that has
# never written is invisible in it. So it is declared here, in a tracked file,
# and the floor on this file's size is pinned separately in
# scripts/usage_journal_producer_floor.tsv. Shrinking the roster to make the
# gate pass therefore takes TWO edits in one change, both visible in review.
# HOW A PRODUCER IS IDENTIFIED IN THE JOURNAL, AND WHAT IS MEASURED VS PINNED
# A record carries no producer field. The only per-producer discriminators
# available are `session_id` and `purpose`, so each row declares which one it
# is matched by:
#   session_prefix   the record's session_id starts with match_value AND its
#                    purpose equals this row's purpose. Both, because a
#                    producer writing the wrong purpose is also a defect.
#   purpose          the record's purpose equals match_value. Used only where
#                    no prefix exists to match on.
# MEASURED, not assumed:
#   cm051_ostler_fda_ingest   PREFIX measured from vendor/ostler_fda/pwg_ingest.py:50
#                             (_USAGE_SESSION_ID = f"ostler-fda-ingest-{uuid4}").
#                             ⚠️ THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY THE WRITER WAS NOT VENDORED, and
#                             that stopped being true when the re-vendor landed (#1305).
#                             Re-measured on the tree that ships: vendor/ostler_fda holds
#                             36 files, 2 of which reference the journal --
#                             usage_journal.py itself, and pwg_ingest.py, which imports
#                             record_usage at :36-37 and calls it at :72.
#                             tests/test_vendored_fda_writes_the_usage_journal.sh proves
#                             it BY EXECUTION ("RUNNING the vendored producer writes a
#                             record"), not by grep.
#                             This correction matters because the old text was a BENIGN
#                             EXPLANATION FOR AN ABSENCE: a reader seeing this probe RED
#                             would have read "fda is dark, expected" and moved on, when
#                             a RED now means something else entirely. That is the same
#                             failure #1141 fixed inside the probe itself.
#   cm044_wiki_compiler       the worked example in the contract's own THE
#                             RECORD section: "cm044-compile-2026-08-24T..."
#   oa_daemon_chat            oa crates/zeroclaw-config/src/cost/tracker.rs:32
#                             session_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string().
#                             A BARE UUID -- there is no prefix to match on,
#                             which is why this row matches on purpose and the
#                             others do not. Checked before assuming.
# PINNED BY THIS FILE, not yet observable, because the producer is not written:
#   cm048_conversation_extract, cm041_identity_resolution. Their prefixes
#   follow the contract's own naming of the CM044 example. If either lands
#   writing a DIFFERENT session_id prefix, this gate reports it ABSENT and goes
#   RED, and the fix is to correct the row in the same change that wires the
#   producer. That direction is deliberate: a false RED here is one line of
#   review, and a false GREEN is a customer being shown a cost figure that is
#   wrong in the flattering direction.
# status
#   required   must appear in the journal, or the gate FAILS naming it.
#   dormant    declared by the contract but not owed yet, with the contract's
#              own reason quoted in provenance. Reported, never failed on. A
#              dormant producer that DOES appear is a note, not a fault.
# Fields are TAB separated. No field may contain a tab.
# producer_id
